7.01.b:
### Hold it → side in 3 steps
- **Step 1 — orient**
  - Articular condyles **down**, trochlea (patellar groove) **toward you**, notch **away** from you
    [[FIG: Fig 7.1 · 7.01
- **Step 2 — find lateral**
  - **Lateral trochlear facet** → higher (more proximal), wider, more prominent → the lateral buttress against patellar dislocation
  - Lateral condyle → **popliteal groove** on its outer surface
- **Step 3 — find medial**
  - **Adductor tubercle** → bump at the top of the medial supracondylar ridge
  - Medial condyle → larger, longer, projects further distally (with shaft vertical) and posteriorly
- **Side rule** → put it on your own thigh, trochlea forward → medial side faces midline → that is the side
- Trochlea seen end-on → **groove line** (cartilage sulcus) separates trochlear facet from condyle on each side
  [[FIG: Fig 7.2 · 7.01

EXAM PEARL
- "How do you know it is right?" → **lateral facet of trochlea is higher and wider** → so this side is lateral
- Confirm with **adductor tubercle** → medial

### Point & say — the two sides are mirrors
- Rule → **main bump → collateral ligament just above and behind it** (both sides)
  [[FIG: Fig 7.3 · 7.01
- Medial → **AT on top, ME in front and below, GT at the back**; lateral → **"LCL behind, Pop in front and below"**

| Point to | Medial side | Lateral side |
|---|---|---|
| Main bump (epicondyle) | **ME** → **sMCL** just above and behind | **LE** → **FCL** just above and behind |
| Top bump | **AT** → adductor magnus | — |
| Back | **GT** → medial gastrocnemius; POL just in front of it | Lateral gastrocnemius; plantaris higher up |
| Saddle / groove | **AT–ME saddle** → **MPFL** | **Popliteal sulcus**, front end → **popliteus** |
| Debated spot | — | **ALL** → around LE |

CLINICAL PEARL — trochlea and lateral epicondyle
- Trochlear dysplasia → **crossing sign** on a true lateral X-ray → present in 96% of dysplastic knees (Dejour 1994)
- Instability factors → dysplasia, patella alta, **TT–TG ≥20 mm** → each found in only 3–6.5% of normal knees
- **Lateral epicondyle** → ITB rubs over it near 30° of flexion → **ITB friction syndrome** in runners → pain on the LE, not on the joint line

### Point & say — intercondylar notch
- **Lateral wall** (medial surface of lateral condyle) → **ACL**, posterior part
  - **Resident's ridge** (lateral intercondylar ridge) → ACL is behind it
  - **Bifurcate ridge** → separates AM bundle (proximal) from PL bundle (distal)
- **Medial wall** (lateral surface of medial condyle) → **PCL**, anterior part, close to cartilage
- Roof → **Blumensaat line** on lateral X-ray

MUST-KNOW
- ACL → **back** of the **lateral** wall
- PCL → **front** of the **medial** wall

7.02.b:
### Hold it → side
- Apex (inferior pole) **down**, articular surface (posterior) **toward you**
- Vertical ridge → two facets → **lateral facet larger and wider**
  [[FIG: Fig 7.4 · 7.02
- Put it back on your own knee (articular surface to the femur) → larger facet goes **outside** → side
- Laid on the table on its articular surface → tilts toward the **lateral** (larger) facet

### Point & say
- **Seven facets** → medial and lateral each split into superior, middle, inferior (6) + **odd facet** (far medial)
  - Odd facet → contacts only in **deep flexion** (sitting on the floor)
- Upper part → articular; **apex** → non-articular → **patellar tendon**
- Base (superior border) → quadriceps tendon
- Superomedial border → **MPFL** (upper half) + MQTFL into quadriceps tendon
- Thickest articular cartilage in the body → up to **5 mm**
- Bipartite patella → **superolateral** fragment → not a fracture
  [[FIG: Fig 7.5 · 7.02

EXAM PEARL
- Patella engages trochlea at **≈20°**, fully by **≈40°** of flexion
- MPFL → 50–60% of restraint to lateral translation at **0–30°**

- Bursae around the knee → sagittal section
  [[FIG: Fig 7.6 · 7.02

- **Superficial infrapatellar** bursa → in front of the patellar tendon → upright kneeling → **clergyman's knee**
- Egg-shaped swelling **on** the patella with a normal joint → bursa, not effusion

7.03.t: Proximal Tibia & Fibula — Bone in Hand
7.03.b:
### Hold it → side
- Plateau **up**, **tibial tuberosity** facing **away** from you (anterior)
- **Medial plateau** → larger, oval, **concave**
- **Lateral plateau** → smaller, round, **convex**
- **Fibular facet** → under the lateral condyle, posterolateral
- **Gerdy's tubercle** → anterolateral → iliotibial band
- Side rule → tuberosity forward, find the fibular facet → that side is lateral

### Point & say — the plateau map (front → back)
- Order → **M-A-L | L-M-P** → see the pin map
  [[FIG: Fig 7.7, 7.8 · 7.03
  - **M** → anterior horn of **medial** meniscus (most anterior)
  - **A** → **ACL** footprint
  - **L** → anterior horn of **lateral** meniscus (fibres blend with ACL)
  - Tibial spines (medial and lateral intercondylar tubercles)
  - **L** → posterior horn of lateral meniscus
  - **M** → posterior horn of medial meniscus
  - **P** → **PCL** → posterior sulcus, below the joint line
- ACL tibial centre → **≈7.5 mm medial** to anterior horn of lateral meniscus; **≈7 mm anterior** to PCL
- Posterior root of medial meniscus → **≈8 mm** from PCL → protect it when drilling PCL tunnel

### Point & say — around the tibia
- Muscle map of tibia and fibula → origins red, insertions blue
  [[FIG: Fig 7.9 · 7.03
- **Tibial tuberosity** → patellar tendon; ≈3 cm below joint line
- **Gerdy's tubercle** → ITB; also origin of tibialis anterior
- **Medial flare** → pes anserinus (Sartorius, Gracilis, semiTendinosus → "Say Grace before Tea")
  - Deep and posterior to pes → **distal sMCL** (≈6 cm below joint)
- **Posteromedial groove** → semimembranosus (direct arm)

- **Posterior surface** → popliteus (triangle above soleal line) → **soleal line** → soleus
- **Posterior intercondylar fossa** → PCL (champagne-glass drop-off)

CLINICAL PEARL — around the tibia
- **Tibial tuberosity** apophysis → **Osgood–Schlatter** → traction apophysitis in adolescent athletes → tender, prominent tubercle
- **Pes anserine bursa** → between the pes tendons and the distal sMCL → tender **below** the joint line, over the pes → not the meniscus

### Point & say — fibular head
- Map → three pins on the head + one danger band on the neck (pin map above)
- **LCL** → lateral fibular head, ≈8 mm behind its anterior margin
- **Biceps femoris** → fibular head, wraps around LCL ("V" on sagittal MRI)
- **Styloid (apex)** → popliteofibular ligament, fabellofibular, arcuate ligaments
- **Fibular neck** → **common peroneal nerve** winds around it → palpable
- Soleus → posterior fibular head; peroneus longus → lateral head and shaft

PITFALL
- Fibular head avulsion on X-ray → **arcuate sign** → posterolateral corner until proved otherwise
- Do not confuse it with a Segond fracture → lateral **tibial** rim (ALL / capsule) → ACL

7.04.b:
### ACL
| Item | ACL |
|---|---|
| Femur | Posterior part of medial surface of lateral condyle, behind resident's ridge |
| Tibia | Anterior intercondylar area, between the anterior horns |
| Bundles | **AM** (tight in flexion) + **PL** (tight in extension) → named by tibial site |
| Size | ≈32–35 mm long, ≈10 mm wide → ≈30% smaller than PCL |
| Function | Primary restraint to **anterior tibial translation**; PL → rotation (pivot shift) |
| Blood | **Middle genicular** artery |

- Femoral centre → ≈1.7 mm proximal to **bifurcate ridge**, ≈6 mm posterior to **resident's ridge**
  [[FIG: Fig 7.10 · 7.04
- **IDEAL** femoral point → Isometric, Direct fibres, Eccentric, Anatomic, Low tension
  [[FIG: Fig 7.11 · 7.04
- X-ray link → normal ACL parallel to or steeper than **Blumensaat line**

CLINICAL PEARL — ACL
- Swelling within **hours** of a twist → haemarthrosis → ACL tear in **72%** (Noyes 1980); swelling the next day → meniscus
- **Pivot shift** → needs an intact **MCL** (valgus hinge) + **ITB** → near 30° the ITB passes behind the knee axis → pulls the tibia back → the "clunk"
- **Bone bruise** → **lateral femoral condyle** (middle) + **posterolateral tibial plateau** → seen in >80% of ACL tears (Levine 2013)

### PCL
| Item | PCL |
|---|---|
| Femur | Anterior part of lateral surface of medial condyle, close to cartilage |
| Tibia | Posterior intercondylar fossa → **≈1–1.5 cm below** joint line |
| Bundles | **AL** (larger, stronger, tight in flexion) + **PM** (tight in extension) |
| Meniscofemoral | **Humphrey** → anterior to PCL; **Wrisberg** → posterior to PCL |
| Function | Primary restraint to **posterior tibial translation** |
| Danger | Popliteal artery ≈7 mm behind the footprint → farther in flexion (≈10 mm at 100°) |

- Femoral landmarks → **trochlear point**, **medial arch point**, **medial bifurcate ridge** (AL vs PM)
  [[FIG: Fig 7.12 · 7.04
- Tibial landmark → **champagne-glass drop-off** → guide-pin target

HIGH YIELD
- PCL → ≈30% larger and stronger than ACL
- Single-bundle PCL reconstruction → **AL bundle**
- Both cruciates → intra-articular but **extrasynovial**

CLINICAL PEARL — PCL
- Normal **step-off** at 90° → medial plateau ≈10 mm **in front of** the MFC → grade I <5 mm, II 6–10 mm (flush), III >10 mm (tibia behind the condyle)
- Grade III → think **PLC** as well → dial test at 30° and 90°
- Posterior capsule often tears → blood tracks into the **calf** → the knee itself may look only mildly swollen (Handbook)

7.05.b:
### Layers (Warren & Marshall)
| Layer | Contents |
|---|---|
| 1 | Deep (crural) fascia + **sartorius** |
| Between 1 and 2 | **Gracilis + semitendinosus** (harvest plane) |
| 2 | **Superficial MCL**, MPFL, posteromedial structures |
| 3 | Capsule + **deep MCL** (meniscofemoral + meniscotibial) |
| 2 + 3 posteriorly | **POL** (fused) |

### Point & say — the attachments (LaPrade numbers)
- **sMCL femur** → 3.2 mm proximal + 4.8 mm posterior to **medial epicondyle**
  [[FIG: Fig 7.13, 7.14 · 7.05
- **sMCL tibia** → two sites → proximal (soft tissue, ≈1 cm below joint) + **distal ≈61 mm** below joint, under pes
- sMCL length → ≈95 mm → main restraint to **valgus**, mostly at **30°**
- **Deep MCL** → short, attached to medial meniscus → why MM is less mobile
- **POL** → 7.7 mm distal + 6.4 mm posterior to **adductor tubercle**
- **MPFL femur** → 1.9 mm anterior + 3.8 mm distal to **adductor tubercle** → saddle between AT and ME
  [[FIG: Fig 7.15 · 7.05
- **Semimembranosus** → remember **3 main arms** → **direct** (posteromedial tibia), **anterior** (under sMCL), **OPL** (to lateral capsule)
  - Full count → 5 arms (MRI) to 8 attachments (dissection) → do not list them unless asked

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "show me the MCL"
- Touch the **medial epicondyle** → sMCL starts just above and behind it
- Run down ≈6 cm → distal tibial attachment, deep and behind the **pes**
- Function → main **valgus** restraint, mostly at **30°**; POL in extension
- Heals well (extracapsular, vascular) → brace; old femoral avulsion → **Pellegrini–Stieda**

CLINICAL PEARL — MCL
- Valgus opening at **30° only** → MCL; opening at **0°** too → MCL + POL/capsule ± cruciate
- Distal sMCL can flip **over the pes** → **Stener-like lesion** → cannot heal back → repair (Corten 2010)
  - Clue → stable in extension, no firm end point at 30° → not a simple grade 2

### MPFL and Schöttle point
- MPFL → fan-shaped → ≈2.5 cm wide at patella → ≈12 mm at femur; ≈5.5 cm long
  [[FIG: Fig 7.16 · 7.05
- Medial restraints → **proximal** (MPFL, MQTFL) + **distal** (MPTL, MPML)
- Layer → **deep to medial retinaculum**, superficial to synovium → graft plane
- **Schöttle point** (true lateral X-ray, posterior condyles overlapped)
  [[FIG: Fig 7.17 · 7.05
  - 1 mm **anterior** to the posterior cortex line
  - 2.5 mm **distal** to the posterior origin of the medial condyle
  - **Proximal** to the most posterior point of Blumensaat line

PITFALL
- Lectures quote "1 cm proximal to ME" and "4 mm distal to AT" → both land in the same saddle
- In children → physis is close → many use **adductor magnus** sling, no femoral tunnel

CLINICAL PEARL — MPFL tear site
- After lateral patellar dislocation → MPFL tears at the **patella 47%**, **femur 26%**, both 13% (MRI of 195 knees, Guerrero 2009)
- **Femoral avulsion** → more redislocation without surgery (Sillanpää 2009)
- Bone bruise → **medial patellar facet + lateral femoral condyle** → a dislocation that reduced itself

- Technique details → Operative notes; here → **what, where, why**

### Arthroscopy portals
| Portal | At risk | Why | Safe trick |
|---|---|---|---|
| Anteromedial / anterolateral | **Infrapatellar branch (IPBSN)**, fat pad, anterior horns | IPBSN crosses below patella, medial → lateral | Stay close to the tendon; horizontal skin cut |
| Posteromedial | **Saphenous nerve + vein** | Run with sartorius, behind sMCL | Knee 90°, transilluminate, needle first, stay in front of the vein |
| Posterolateral | **CPN** | Nerve lies **behind biceps** | Knee 90°, portal **in front of biceps**, behind LCL |
| Superolateral / superomedial | Quadriceps, SLGA | — | Above the patella, through the tendon edge |

### Arthroscopic procedures
| Procedure | At risk | Why | Safe trick |
|---|---|---|---|
| Inside-out repair, **lateral** meniscus | **CPN** | Behind biceps, near the posterolateral capsule | Incision behind LCL, in front of biceps; retractor between **lateral gastrocnemius and capsule** |
| Inside-out repair, **medial** meniscus | **Saphenous nerve + vein** | Behind sMCL with sartorius | Incision behind sMCL; retractor in front of medial gastrocnemius, deep to sartorius |
| All-inside, posterior horns near PCL | **Popliteal artery / bundle** | Bundle is just behind the posterior capsule | Depth limiter; device path hit the bundle in ≈29% of simulated passes near the PCL |
| Hamstring harvest | **Saphenous** (IPBSN + sartorial branch) | Nerve runs with gracilis 7–12 cm above insertion | Oblique incision; numbness in up to ≈74% |
| ACL femoral tunnel (AM portal) | **CPN**, posterior wall | Pin exits posterolaterally | **Hyperflex ≥120°** → pin 44 mm from CPN (23 mm at 70°) |
| PCL tibial tunnel | **Popliteal artery** | ≈7 mm behind the footprint | Flex 90–100°, curette on the pin tip, posteromedial portal |
| PLC reconstruction | **CPN** | Behind biceps, around fibular neck | Find biceps first → neurolysis before the fibular tunnel |

### Open knee surgery
| Procedure | At risk | Why | Safe trick |
|---|---|---|---|
| TKA medial parapatellar | **IPBSN** | Crosses the incision | Expect numbness lateral to the scar → warn the patient |
| TKA lateral release | **Superior lateral genicular artery** | Runs above the lateral retinaculum | Release below it if possible → patellar blood supply |
| TKA tibial / posterior cuts | **Popliteal artery**, MCL | Artery behind posterior tibia; flexion does **not** move it away at the baseplate level | Posterior retractor; protect MCL with the saw |
| TKA, valgus ≥12° or flexion contracture | **CPN** (palsy ≈0.3%) | Stretched with correction | Flex knee post-op if signs; release dressing |
| HTO opening wedge | Popliteal artery; sMCL, pes | Behind posterior cortex | Knee flexed, retractor on posterior cortex; release distal sMCL |
| HTO closing wedge / fibular cut | **CPN, DPN** | Danger band 2–3.5 cm below fibular tip | Cut the fibula well below the neck |

### Leg — in brief
- **Tibial nail** → entry → IPBSN, patellar tendon; proximal oblique screws too long → **CPN**; distal screws → SPN, anterior tibial bundle
- **Posterolateral plateau approach** → **anterior tibial artery** pierces the membrane **≈46 mm** below the lateral plateau → limit distal dissection
- **Spanning ex-fix** (knee dislocation) → pins well away from the joint (Handbook: >10 cm) → out of the capsule and of future graft tunnels

- sMCL femoral attachment? | Just proximal and posterior to the medial epicondyle

- FCL femoral attachment? | Just proximal and posterior to the lateral epicondyle
